---
title: "Code Style"
---

14 requirement(s) in this category.

### STY-001 — 100-character line limit {#sec-sty-001}

**Mathlib + PhysLean** · Level **SHALL**

Lines SHALL NOT be longer than 100 characters.

**Acceptance criteria**

- No source line exceeds 100 characters.
- The style linter reports no line-length violations.

**Rationale.** Short lines stay readable on small screens, in narrow windows, and in side-by-side diffs.

**Verify.** lake exe lint-style   (physlean: ./scripts/lint-style.sh)

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-002 — Declarations flush-left {#sec-sty-002}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

All declarations SHALL appear flush-left; opening a `namespace` or `section` SHALL NOT indent its contents.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Top-level declarations start in column 1.
- Contents of namespaces/sections are not indented.

**Rationale.** Flat, flush-left structure keeps files scannable regardless of section nesting.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-003 — Whitespace around operators and binders {#sec-sty-003}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

There SHALL be a space on both sides of `:`, `:=`, and infix operators, and a space after binders. When a line is broken, the operator SHALL go before the break, not at the start of the next line.

**Acceptance criteria**

- `:`, `:=`, and infix operators are surrounded by single spaces.
- Line breaks keep the operator on the preceding line.

**Rationale.** Uniform spacing makes expressions legible and diffs minimal.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-004 — Proof and continuation indentation {#sec-sty-004}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

A proof SHALL be indented 2 spaces after the theorem statement. When a theorem statement spans multiple lines, continuation lines SHALL be indented 4 spaces (the proof is still only 2).

**Acceptance criteria**

- Proof bodies are indented 2 spaces.
- Multi-line statement continuations are indented 4 spaces.

**Rationale.** A fixed indentation scheme separates statement from proof at a glance.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-005 — `by` at end of the preceding line {#sec-sty-005}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

`by` SHALL be placed at the end of the line preceding the tactic block, never on a line by itself. For a short `have`, the justifying `by` goes on the same line.

**Acceptance criteria**

- No line consists solely of `by`.
- `by` terminates the line before the first tactic.

**Rationale.** Keeping `by` on the prior line avoids an orphan token and a wasted line.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-006 — Use `fun … ↦ …`; `λ` is disallowed {#sec-sty-006}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

Anonymous functions SHALL be written with the `fun` keyword and the `↦` arrow. The `λ` lambda notation is disallowed in Mathlib.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Anonymous functions use `fun … ↦ …`.
- No `λ` appears in submitted code.

**Rationale.** One spelling of anonymous functions keeps the source uniform.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-007 — Tactic-block focusing dots and one-tactic-per-line {#sec-sty-007}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHOULD**

Within a tactic block, when multiple goals arise each SHOULD be preceded by a focusing dot `·` (not indented), and generally one tactic SHOULD be written per line; newlines are preferred over semicolons even for short sequences.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Multiple goals are handled under focusing dots `·`.
- Tactics are one per line except for short single-idea sequences.

**Rationale.** Focusing dots make the goal structure explicit and keep proofs reviewable.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-008 — No empty lines inside declarations {#sec-sty-008}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

Empty lines inside a declaration are disallowed and enforced by a linter; a comment SHALL be used instead of a blank line to separate parts of a proof.

**Acceptance criteria**

- No blank line appears inside a declaration.
- Separation within a proof is done with comments.

**Rationale.** Blank lines inside a declaration confuse the boundary between declarations; comments carry more information.

**Verify.** The `empty lines inside declarations` linter.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-009 — Standard variable-letter conventions {#sec-sty-009}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHOULD**

Variables SHOULD follow the usual letter conventions: `u v w` for universes; `α β γ` for generic types; `x y z` for elements; `h h₁` for hypotheses; `p q r` for predicates/relations; `s t` for sets/lists; `m n k` for naturals; `i j k` for integers. Mathematical types use conventional letters (`G` group, `R` ring, `K`/`𝕜` field, `E` vector space).

**Acceptance criteria**

- Variable names follow the conventional letter roles.

**Rationale.** Conventional names let a reader infer the role of a variable immediately.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-010 — Safe Unicode use {#sec-sty-010}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHOULD**

Special Unicode characters, especially mathematical symbols, SHOULD be used where they develop good notation, but code SHALL avoid characters that change text direction, invisible characters (other than spaces and newlines), and characters that modify other characters.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Notation uses standard mathematical Unicode.
- No direction-changing, invisible, or modifier characters are present.

**Rationale.** Good notation aids readability; unsafe Unicode causes subtle rendering and security problems.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-011 — Explicit argument and return types {#sec-sty-011}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHALL**

The type of every argument SHALL be given explicitly, and the return type of every declaration SHALL be stated.

**Acceptance criteria**

- All arguments carry explicit types.
- Every declaration states its return type.

**Rationale.** Explicit types make declarations self-documenting and stable under refactoring.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-012 — Definition transparency defaults {#sec-sty-012}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHOULD**

Definitions SHOULD be `semireducible` (the `def` default). `irreducible_def` SHOULD be used only when a documented necessity from profiling requires it; prefer a type-synonym structure wrapper over `irreducible`. Reliance on `erw`, or `rfl` after `simp`, indicates missing API.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Definitions are semireducible unless profiling documents otherwise.
- `irreducible_def` uses carry a profiling justification.

**Rationale.** Transparency choices have large downstream effects on elaboration and should be deliberate and profiled.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-013 — Deprecate rather than delete {#sec-sty-013}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHOULD**

When renaming or removing a public declaration, the old name SHOULD be kept with an `@[deprecated]` attribute carrying a deprecation date (a renamed declaration via a deprecated `alias`); a deprecation without a replacement needs a message. Deprecated declarations MAY be deleted after six months.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Renamed/removed public decls retain a dated `@[deprecated]` alias.
- Replacement-less deprecations carry a message.

**Rationale.** Deprecation windows protect downstream users from sudden breakage.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>

---

### STY-014 — Performance awareness and benchmarking {#sec-sty-014}

**Mathlib** · Level **SHOULD**

Authors SHOULD be aware of the performance impact of a contribution; changes to classes, instances, `simp` lemmas, imports, or definitions, and non-trivial refactors, SHOULD be benchmarked. Contributions SHOULD NOT cause significant performance regressions.

**Acceptance criteria**

- Performance-sensitive changes are benchmarked.
- No significant regression is introduced.

**Rationale.** Mathlib compiles as one library; local slowdowns become everyone's slowdown.

**Verify.** Comment `!bench` on the PR to run the benchmarking infrastructure.

**Source.** <https://leanprover-community.github.io/contribute/style.html>
